hunk_reviews.judgment: The new root injectable reads APP_ID and stores module counters keyed by prefix, omitting the default ng ID. Both exact minimum current services retain that application distinction; main uses a Map, 21.x an object, and both later add an optional random infix. The legacy historical counter model does not become part of that service through ancestry or provider presence. Preserve owned manual construction and fix the distinct generated namespace locally; actual node/ARIA coexistence is mandatory.

The public CDK a11y barrel exports the underscore helper for upstream infrastructure. That export does not authorize a new legacy facade export, a CDK fork or an owned private upstream import under the repository policy. The maintained peers continue to own their service. All current owned product bytes are checked unchanged and contain no _IdGenerator dependency.

The API guard records the new underscore class and Angular factory/provider metadata. No corresponding historical add-on API or compiler metadata is mirrored. The refusal to adopt the private service does not waive the required actual mixed-generation identity behavior, and it does not raise the advertised minimum peers.

source_conclusion: Do not transplant the complete three-file CDK underscore ID-generator service, barrel or API guard into this legacy add-on. It is current CDK infrastructure, not a historical legacy API or an owned stable public dependency. Its APP_ID/root-service/per-prefix state is independently owned by current peers; owned historical counters neither invoke it nor share its counters. Earlier ancestry and counter-retention arguments therefore did not prove mixed-generation uniqueness. The locally owned suffix/prefix repairs address that reachable collision without introducing an injection requirement into historical manual constructors or promising the younger private service API. Require the complete actual packed mixed-generation identity case: both creation orders, exact unique nodes, ARIA references, explicit inputs, snack modal ownership and cleanup. This does not promise uniqueness across independently loaded copies of the same legacy library, adversarial explicit IDs or new APP_ID/randomization APIs. Full floor/consumer and global release gates remain separate.
